import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    # Costs
    "setup_cost": 121.0782541217011,
    "startup_cost": 69.65555018358044,
    "holding_cost": {0: 1.196682091019819, 1: 1.146459407730801},
    "backlog_cost": {0: 7.384397449671641, 1: 6.58642780982885},
    # Demand [product][period]
    "demand": {
        0: {0: 22.28694038228271, 1: 15.40553617195959,
            2: 16.19622794603683, 3: 23.77133167016131},
        1: {0: 16.51020937307772, 1: 15.41395287058592,
            2: 23.98409764196543, 3: 18.84683167137874},
    },
    # Machine capacities
    "capacity": {0: 63.4339018881536, 1: 67.51600987446864},
    # Startup times
    "startup_time": {0: 7.917022863645049, 1: 7.682853596177669},
    # Sets
    "products": [0, 1],
    "machines": [0, 1],
    "periods": [0, 1, 2, 3],
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    products = d["products"]
    machines = d["machines"]
    periods = d["periods"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=products)
    model.M = pyo.Set(initialize=machines)
    model.T = pyo.Set(initialize=periods)

    # Production quantity (continuous, non-negative)
    # "Production quantities, inventory, and backlog must be non-negative."
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                      within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Inventory
    # "Production quantities, inventory, and backlog must be non-negative."
    model.I = pyo.Var(model.P, model.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Backlog
    # "Production quantities, inventory, and backlog must be non-negative."
    model.B = pyo.Var(model.P, model.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Assignment binary: machine m assigned to product p in period t
    # assumption: separate assign[m,p,t] and setup[m,p,t] binaries
    model.assign = pyo.Var(model.M, model.P, model.T, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Setup binary: production run of product p on machine m in period t
    # "The setup cost is 121.0782541217011 per production run"
    model.setup = pyo.Var(model.M, model.P, model.T, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Startup binary: machine m starts up for product p in period t
    # "The startup cost is 69.65555018358044 per startup."
    model.startup = pyo.Var(model.M, model.P, model.T, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimize total cost
    # "Minimize the total production costs, which include setup costs,
    #  startup costs, inventory holding costs, and backlogging costs"
    def obj_rule(m):
        setup_term = sum(d["setup_cost"] * m.setup[mm, pp, tt]
                         for mm in m.M for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        startup_term = sum(d["startup_cost"] * m.startup[mm, pp, tt]
                           for mm in m.M for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        hold_term = sum(d["holding_cost"][pp] * m.I[pp, tt]
                        for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        back_term = sum(d["backlog_cost"][pp] * m.B[pp, tt]
                        for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        return setup_term + startup_term + hold_term + back_term

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Demand balance
    # "The total production, inventory, and backlog must balance customer
    #  demand for each product in each period."
    def balance_rule(m, p, t):
        prev_I = m.I[p, t - 1] if t - 1 in m.T else 0
        prev_B = m.B[p, t - 1] if t - 1 in m.T else 0
        return (prev_I - prev_B
                + sum(m.x[mm, p, t] for mm in m.M)
                - m.I[p, t] + m.B[p, t]
                == d["demand"][p][t])

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.P, model.T, rule=balance_rule)

    # Machine capacity with startup time consumption
    # "The startup time for Machine 0 is ... and for Machine 1, is ..."
    # "Each machine has a limited capacity"
    # assumption: startup time consumes capacity
    def cap_rule(m, mm, t):
        return (sum(m.x[mm, pp, t] for pp in m.P)
                + d["startup_time"][mm] * sum(m.startup[mm, pp, t]
                                              for pp in m.P)
                <= d["capacity"][mm])

    model.capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.T, rule=cap_rule)

    # One product per machine per period
    # "Each machine can produce only one product at a time in any given period."
    def one_prod_rule(m, mm, t):
        return sum(m.assign[mm, pp, t] for pp in m.P) <= 1

    model.one_product = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.T, rule=one_prod_rule)

    # assign <= setup
    # assumption: separate assign[m,p,t] and setup[m,p,t] binaries with
    #  assign <= setup
    def assign_setup_rule(m, mm, pp, t):
        return m.assign[mm, pp, t] <= m.setup[mm, pp, t]

    model.assign_setup = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                                        rule=assign_setup_rule)

    # prod <= bigM * assign, bigM = capacity
    # assumption: prod <= bigM*assign with bigM = machine capacity cap[m]
    def prod_link_rule(m, mm, pp, t):
        return m.x[mm, pp, t] <= d["capacity"][mm] * m.assign[mm, pp, t]

    model.prod_link = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                                     rule=prod_link_rule)

    # Startup logic: startup only if not producing same product previous period
    # "A machine can only be started up for a product if it was not producing
    #  that product in the previous period."
    # startup[m,p,t] >= setup[m,p,t] - setup[m,p,t-1]
    def startup_rule(m, mm, pp, t):
        prev = m.setup[mm, pp, t - 1] if t - 1 in m.T else 0
        return m.startup[mm, pp, t] >= m.setup[mm, pp, t] - prev

    model.startup_logic = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                                         rule=startup_rule)

    return model

    # Setup / assignment binary y[m,p,t]

    model.y = pyo.Var(model.M, model.P, model.T, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Startup binary s[m,p,t]
    # "Production and startup decisions are binary (either 0 or 1)."
    model.s = pyo.Var(model.M, model.P, model.T, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimize total production costs
    # "Minimize the total production costs, which include setup costs,
    #  startup costs, inventory holding costs, and backlogging costs"
    def obj_rule(m):
        setup = sum(d["setup_cost"] * m.y[mm, pp, tt]
                    for mm in m.M for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        startup = sum(d["startup_cost"] * m.s[mm, pp, tt]
                      for mm in m.M for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        holding = sum(d["holding_cost"][pp] * m.I[pp, tt]
                      for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        backlog = sum(d["backlog_cost"][pp] * m.B[pp, tt]
                      for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        return setup + startup + holding + backlog

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Balance equality
    # "The total production, inventory, and backlog must balance customer
    #  demand for each product in each period."
    def balance_rule(m, pp, tt):
        prev_I = m.I[pp, tt - 1] if tt > 0 else 0
        prev_B = m.B[pp, tt - 1] if tt > 0 else 0
        return (prev_I - prev_B
                + sum(m.x[mm, pp, tt] for mm in m.M)
                - m.I[pp, tt] + m.B[pp, tt]
                == d["demand"][pp][tt])

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.P, model.T, rule=balance_rule)

    # One product per machine per period
    # "Each machine can produce only one product at a time in any given period."
    def one_product_rule(m, mm, tt):
        return sum(m.y[mm, pp, tt] for pp in m.P) <= 1

    model.one_product = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.T, rule=one_product_rule)

    # Production link: x[m,p,t] <= cap[m] * y[m,p,t]
    # assumption: bigM = machine capacity cap[m]
    def prod_link_rule(m, mm, pp, tt):
        return m.x[mm, pp, tt] <= d["capacity"][mm] * m.y[mm, pp, tt]

    model.prod_link = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                                     rule=prod_link_rule)

    # Startup definition: s[m,p,t] = y[m,p,t]*(1 - y[m,p,t-1])
    # "A machine can only be started up for a product if it was not
    #  producing that product in the previous period."
    # Linearised: s >= y[t] - y[t-1]; s <= y[t]; s <= 1 - y[t-1]
    def startup_upper_rule(m, mm, pp, tt):
        return m.s[mm, pp, tt] <= m.y[mm, pp, tt]

    model.startup_upper = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                                         rule=startup_upper_rule)

    def startup_prev_rule(m, mm, pp, tt):
        if tt == 0:
            return m.s[mm, pp, tt] <= 1
        return m.s[mm, pp, tt] <= 1 - m.y[mm, pp, tt - 1]

    model.startup_prev = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                                        rule=startup_prev_rule)

    def startup_lower_rule(m, mm, pp, tt):
        if tt == 0:
            return m.s[mm, pp, tt] >= m.y[mm, pp, tt]
        return m.s[mm, pp, tt] >= m.y[mm, pp, tt] - m.y[mm, pp, tt - 1]

    model.startup_lower = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                                         rule=startup_lower_rule)

    # Capacity with startup time consumption
    # "The startup time for Machine 0 is ... and for Machine 1, it is ..."
    # "Each machine has a limited capacity"
    def capacity_rule(m, mm, tt):
        return (sum(m.x[mm, pp, tt] for pp in m.P)
                + d["startup_time"][mm] * sum(m.s[mm, pp, tt] for pp in m.P)
                <= d["capacity"][mm])

    model.capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.T, rule=capacity_rule)

    return model
